usage.notes: Cornerstone3D is a browser medical-imaging framework. Local DICOM can be supported without a network; DICOMweb and remote studies require authenticated network access. Patient imaging must remain separated from public reference anatomy and must never be uploaded to third-party services implicitly.

license.scope: The Cornerstone3D software repository is MIT licensed. This software license does not grant rights to DICOM studies, patient data, annotations, segmentations, trained models, or third-party codecs/datasets used with it.
license.notes: Retain the MIT copyright and permission notice. Track imaging data provenance, access permissions, de-identification status, and any third-party codec/model licenses separately.

validation.notes: Cornerstone3D provides rendering, interaction and segmentation-viewing capabilities; use of the framework does not by itself make Panacea a validated diagnostic medical device. Measurement, segmentation, reconstruction and decision-support workflows require separate verification and clinical validation for their intended use.

provenance.notes: Pin package versions and preserve Study/Series/SOP Instance UIDs or equivalent normalized identifiers when handling DICOM. Derived segmentations and surfaces must point back to the source study and transformation history.

adapter.notes: Planned flow: local DICOM or authenticated DICOMweb -> privacy/provenance gate -> Cornerstone loader -> normalized PanaceaImagingStudy -> stack/volume viewport -> optional segmentation/surface export. Keep imaging access behind an adapter rather than calling loaders directly from feature components.

trust.notes: Scores describe suitability as an imaging framework. EvidenceQuality is intentionally low because Cornerstone3D is infrastructure, not biomedical evidence.
